entry: Temporary shelter consisting of sheets of fabric stretched over a frame of poles, designed to be easily dismantled and portable. Smaller tents may be free-standing or pegged to the ground, while large ones are usually anchored with guy ropes tied to stakes or tent pegs. Tents range from bivouac structures for one sleeper to huge [[Circus|circus]] tents. Recreational [[Camping|camping]] tents are either light enough to be carried by backpackers or transported in a vehicle, and most can be pitched or struck in 5 to 25 minutes. First used as portable homes by [[Nomad|nomads]], tents are now mainly used for recreational camping and as temporary shelter. [[Nylon]] and [[Polyester]] are common materials because they are light and absorb less water than [[Cotton]], though they are not necessarily waterproof. Tents have also been increasingly linked with homelessness in the United States, Canada and other regions.

Nepalese-Indian Sherpa mountaineer. On May 29, 1953, Tenzing Norgay and [[Edmund Hillary]] were the first people confirmed to have reached the summit of [[Mount Everest]], during the 1953 British Mount Everest expedition. He had served as a high-altitude porter on British attempts on Everest in the 1930s and took part in an unsuccessful summit attempt in 1947. He settled in [[Darjeeling]], India, and acquired Indian citizenship. From 1954 to 1976 he was the inaugural Director of Field Training at the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute. He wrote the autobiography *Man of Everest*, received the British George Medal and India's Padma Bhushan, and was named by [[Time (magazine)|Time]] one of the 100 most influential people of the 20th century.

Ancient [[Mesoamerica|Mesoamerican]] city about 40 kilometers (25 mi) northeast of [[Mexico City]]. Established around 100 BCE, it became the largest city in the Americas at its zenith, perhaps in the first half of the first millennium CE, with an estimated population of at least 25,000 and likely around 100,000 at its height. Residents lived in multi-family apartment compounds along the Avenue of the Dead, and the city is known for the Pyramid of the Sun, the Pyramid of the Moon and well-preserved [[Mural|murals]]. Teotihuacan exported fine [[Obsidian|obsidian]] tools throughout Mesoamerica. Its major monuments were sacked and systematically burned around 550 CE, possibly related to extreme weather events of 535–536. The later [[Aztecs]] claimed a common ancestry with its inhabitants, although the city predates the Aztec Empire by many centuries. It was designated a [[UNESCO]] [[World Heritage Site]] in 1987.

Chemical element with symbol Tb and atomic number 65. A silvery-white, malleable and ductile rare-earth metal, it is the ninth member of the [[Lanthanide|lanthanide]] series. Terbium is never found free in nature, occurring instead in minerals such as monazite and xenotime. Swedish chemist Carl Gustaf Mosander discovered it in 1843 as an impurity in yttrium oxide, and it was not isolated in pure form until ion exchange techniques were developed. Yttrium, terbium, [[Erbium|erbium]] and [[Ytterbium|ytterbium]] are named after the village of Ytterby in [[Sweden]]. Its trivalent ion is brilliantly [[Fluorescence|fluorescent]], and most of the world's supply goes into green phosphors for fluorescent lamps and television and monitor cathode-ray tubes. Terbium is also part of Terfenol-D, an alloy that expands and contracts more than any other alloy in magnetic fields, used in actuators, naval sonar and sensors. It is considered non-hazardous, though its biological role and toxicity have not been researched in depth.

[[Roman Republic|Roman]] comic playwright of [[Carthage|Carthaginian]] birth. Publius Terentius Afer wrote six comedies based on Greek originals by Menander or Apollodorus of Carystus, all surviving complete and produced between 166 and 160 BC. According to ancient authors he was brought to Rome as a slave, where he gained an education and his freedom, and he then traveled east around the age of 25, dying either of disease in Greece or in a shipwreck. Ancient biographies are often considered speculative, since they were written long after his lifetime. His plays quickly became standard school texts, and he was one of four authors taught to all grammar pupils in the [[Western Roman Empire]]. He kept a central place in European school curricula until the 19th century and influenced [[William Shakespeare]] and [[Molière]].

Australian-American mathematician known for work on [[Partial differential equation|partial differential equations]], [[Combinatorics]], [[Harmonic analysis]] and additive number theory. Born in [[Adelaide]] to Chinese immigrant parents, he won a gold medal at the International Mathematical Olympiad in 1988, aged 13, the youngest gold medallist in the competition's history. He was awarded the [[Fields Medal]] in 2006. With Ben Green he established the Green–Tao theorem, showing that the [[Prime number|primes]] contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. He became the youngest full professor in the history of [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]].

[[Taiwan|Taiwanese]] singer, television personality and musician, widely regarded as one of the most culturally significant figures in the Chinese-speaking world of the 20th century. She recorded more than 1,700 songs in Mandarin, [[Cantonese]], Hokkien, Japanese, English, Italian and other languages. Credited as the Far East's first pop superstar, she helped lay the foundation for modern Chinese [[Pop music|pop]]. She sold over 48 million albums, excluding sales in mainland China. Nicknamed "the soldiers' sweetheart" for entertaining Taiwan's armed forces, she was named by [[Time (magazine)|Time]] in 1986 as one of the seven greatest female singers in the world. She died of an [[Asthma]] attack in [[Thailand]].

[[Spain|Spanish]] Carmelite mystic and reformer. During the [[Counter-Reformation]], she became the central figure of a movement of spiritual and monastic renewal that reformed the Carmelite orders for women and men. With [[John of the Cross|Saint John of the Cross]] she established the Discalced Carmelites, a split formally adopted by papal decree in 1580. Her autobiography, *The Life of Teresa of Jesus*, and her books *The Interior Castle* and *The Way of Perfection* are prominent works of Christian mysticism and meditation. In the autobiography she discerns four stages in the soul's ascent to God. Her paternal grandfather was a converso, and the [[Inquisition]] scrutinized her visions. Canonized in 1622 by Pope Gregory XV, she was declared the first female Doctor of the Church by Pope Paul VI in 1970.

1991 American science fiction action film directed by [[James Cameron]], and a sequel to *The Terminator* (1984). A reprogrammed Terminator is sent back to 1995 to protect the young John Connor from a more advanced killing machine. Co-written by Cameron and William Wisher, it starred [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]], Linda Hamilton and Robert Patrick. With an estimated budget of $94–$102 million, it was the most expensive film made at the time. It grossed $519–$520.9 million, the highest-grossing film of 1991 worldwide, and won four [[Academy Awards]]. It was the first blockbuster to use a computer-generated main character.

Eusocial insect closely related to [[Cockroach|cockroaches]]. Termites consume decaying plant material, generally [[Wood|wood]], leaf litter and soil humus. They are not [[Ant|ants]] but highly derived cockroaches within the order Blattodea, and are often called white ants for their soft, unpigmented workers. About 3,014 extant species are described. Colonies range from a few hundred individuals to several million and are organized into workers, soldiers, and a king and queen. Termites are important decomposers in tropical and subtropical regions, and some species build large mounds that change soil properties. Many species are structural pests that infest timber, and 28 of the most invasive and damaging pest species belong to the genus Coptotermes. The Makiritare of the Alto Orinoco province in [[Venezuela]] eat termites as a delicacy, and they are used in some traditional medicines.

Slender [[Seabird|seabird]] in the subfamily Sterninae of the family Laridae, which also includes [[Gull|gulls]] and skimmers. Terns are lightly built, with long forked tails, narrow wings, long bills and relatively short legs. Most species are pale gray above and white below, with a black cap, though some marsh terns and noddies have dark plumage. They occur worldwide, normally near the [[Sea|sea]], rivers or [[Wetland|wetlands]], and are treated in eleven [[Genus|genera]]. Terns are long-lived and relatively free from natural predators, but most species are declining because of habitat loss, pollution, disturbance and predation by introduced mammals. The Chinese crested tern is critically endangered, and three other species are classed as endangered. The least tern is 23 cm (9 in) long, and the Caspian tern 48–56 cm (19–22 in).

Collection of terracotta sculptures depicting the armies of [[Qin Shi Huang]], the first emperor of China. Buried with the emperor in 210–209 BCE in his mausoleum near [[Xi'an]] in Shaanxi province, it is funerary art meant to protect him in the afterlife. The figures vary in height according to rank, the tallest being the generals, and include warriors, chariots and horses. Estimates from 2007 put the three pits at more than 8,000 soldiers, 130 chariots with 520 horses, and 150 [[Cavalry|cavalry]] horses. Local farmers digging a well discovered the army on March 29, 1974. [[Sima Qian]] described the mausoleum in the Records of the Grand Historian, written about a century after its completion. Work on the tomb began in 246 BCE, soon after the future first emperor, then aged 13, became king of Qin.

Planet composed primarily of [[Silicate|silicate]] rocks or metals, also called a rocky or telluric planet. Terrestrial planets have a solid surface, unlike [[Gas giant|gaseous]] giants, which are composed mostly of hydrogen, helium and water in various physical states. All terrestrial planets in the [[Solar System]] share a basic structure with a central metallic core, mostly [[Iron|iron]], surrounded by a silicate mantle. Their surfaces can show canyons, craters, mountains and volcanoes, depending on erosion and tectonic activity. Their atmospheres are secondary, generated by volcanic outgassing or comet impact debris, unlike the primary atmospheres of giant planets captured from the solar nebula. The International Astronomical Union recognizes four terrestrial planets in the Solar System: [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]], [[Venus]], [[Earth]] and [[Mars]]. Astronomers using the geophysical definition may also count Earth's Moon, Io and sometimes Europa.

[[Dog]] of any of many breeds, originally bred to hunt vermin, typically small, wiry, game and fearless. The name derives from the Latin *terra*, meaning earth, through the Old French *chien terrier*, or "earth dog". Early terriers competed in events such as clearing a pit of rats, and in the 18th century some were crossed with [[Hound|hounds]] to improve their hunting. Other crosses with fighting dogs produced bull and terrier types used in dog-fighting. Today most terriers are kept as companion dogs, and they are divided into five groups. Hunting types such as the Jack Russell Terrier still track quarry underground. Terriers range from the English Toy Terrier, which weighs as little as 2.7 kg (6 lb), to the Airedale Terrier, up to 25 kg (56 lb) or more.

Sub-national areas under U.S. sovereignty, governed as administrative divisions and dependent territories. Five permanently inhabited, unincorporated territories are [[American Samoa]], [[Guam]], the [[Northern Mariana Islands]], [[Puerto Rico]] and the United States Virgin Islands. The other nine, the United States Minor Outlying Islands, are small [[Atoll|atolls]], islands and reefs with no permanent population. Residents cannot vote in United States presidential elections and have only non-voting representation in Congress. Most territories were created to administer newly acquired land and most eventually became states, the most recent being Hawaii in 1959.

American former football quarterback and sports analyst. He played 14 seasons with the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), winning four [[Super Bowl|Super Bowls]] in a six-year period (1974, 1975, 1978 and 1979) and becoming the first quarterback to win three and four. He led the Steelers to eight AFC Central championships and was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1989, in his first year of eligibility. Since 1994 he has been a co-host and analyst on Fox NFL Sunday. He has also released several [[Country music|country music]] albums and appeared in films, including *Failure to Launch*.

American-born British filmmaker, animator and comedian. He created animations for [[Monty Python|Monty Python]]'s Flying Circus, became a performer in the troupe, and was the only member not born in Britain; he became a naturalized British citizen in 1968. He co-directed *Monty Python and the Holy Grail* (1975) before becoming a solo filmmaker. His films, including *Time Bandits* (1981), *Brazil* (1985), *The Fisher King* (1991) and *12 Monkeys* (1995), often use dystopian settings and explore [[Imagination|imagination]] and opposition to bureaucracy and [[Authoritarianism|authoritarianism]]. He received a BAFTA Fellowship for lifetime achievement in 2009.

Stage of education following compulsory education. Definitions vary: it may include all post-compulsory education, all post-secondary education, or be treated as a synonym for higher education. In the International Standard Classification of Education (ISCED), tertiary education refers to levels 5, 6, 7 and 8 of the 2011 version, covering academic education and degree-level technical and professional education. It may culminate in certificates, diplomas or [[Academic degree|academic degrees]], or may be lifelong learning without formal certification. Vocational education beyond secondary school is known as further education in the [[United Kingdom]] and as continuing education in the [[United States]]. [[UNESCO]] describes tertiary education as focused on learning in specialized fields, including academic and higher vocational education.

Early Christian author and theologian from [[Carthage]], in the Roman province of Africa. He was the first Christian author to produce an extensive corpus of Latin Christian literature and is called the "father of Latin Christianity". He was the first Latin writer known to use the term [[Trinity|trinity]], and he wrote against heresies including [[Gnosticism]]. Some of his teachings, such as the subordination of the Son and Spirit to the Father and his condemnation of remarriage for widows, were rejected by the [[Catholic Church]]. Later he was attracted to the New Prophecy of Montanism, though most scholars reject the claim that he was excommunicated. Some sources describe him as [[Berbers|Berber]], while the linguist René Braun suggested Punic origin.

American multinational automotive and clean energy company headquartered in [[Austin, Texas]]. It designs, manufactures and sells battery electric vehicles, stationary battery storage and solar products. Incorporated in July 2003 as Tesla Motors by Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning, the company takes its name from [[Nikola Tesla]]. [[Elon Musk]] led its first funding round in 2004 and was named chief executive officer in 2008. Its models include the Model S, Model X, Model 3, Model Y, Cybertruck and Semi. Since July 2020 it has been the world's most valuable automaker, and in 2024 it led the battery electric vehicle market with a 17.6% share.

SI unit of magnetic flux density, equal to one weber per square meter. Named in honor of [[Nikola Tesla]], it was announced at the 1960 General Conference on Weights and Measures and has the symbol T. A particle carrying one [[Coulomb|coulomb]] and moving at one meter per second perpendicular to a field of one tesla experiences a force of one [[Newton (unit)|newton]], according to the Lorentz force law. One tesla corresponds to 10⁴ G. Earth's surface field is 25000–65000 nT, and a typical refrigerator magnet produces about 5 mT. [[Magnetic resonance imaging]] systems operate at 1.5 to 3 T, and the strongest field produced by a non-destructive magnet reaches 97.4 T.

Covering of a surface, usually a plane, by one or more geometric shapes called tiles, with no overlaps or gaps. Periodic tilings have a repeating pattern and can be classified into 17 wallpaper groups, while a tiling without a repeating pattern is called non-periodic. Only the [[Triangle|equilateral triangle]], [[Square|square]] and [[Hexagon|regular hexagon]] form regular tessellations of identical regular tiles. Sumerians used tessellated clay tiles for wall decorations by about 4000 BC, and tessellations appear in Roman mosaics and in Islamic art such as the [[Alhambra]]. In 1619 [[Johannes Kepler]] made an early documented study of regular and semiregular tessellations. In the 20th century [[M. C. Escher]] used them for artistic effect, and in computer graphics tessellation subdivides [[Polygon|polygon]] meshes into finer triangles to add geometric detail.

Four-dimensional analog of the [[Cube|cube]]. It is bounded by eight cubes, twenty-four squares, thirty-two edges and sixteen vertices, and is one of the six convex regular 4-polytopes. The term hypercube is often used as a synonym for this figure. Charles Howard Hinton introduced the word in his 1888 book *A New Era of Thought*, from Greek roots meaning four and ray. The tesseract has 261 distinct nets, and one unfolding, the Dali cross, appears in [[Salvador Dalí]]'s 1954 painting *Corpus Hypercubus*.

Male gonad in gonochoric animals, including humans, homologous to the [[Ovary|ovary]]. Its primary functions are producing [[Sperm|sperm]] and secreting androgens, mainly [[Testosterone|testosterone]]. Sperm production is controlled by follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) from the anterior [[Pituitary gland|pituitary gland]] and by testosterone produced within the gonads. Human males have two testicles of similar size within the [[Scrotum|scrotum]], and for 85% of men the right one hangs lower than the left. The testes are covered by a tough fibrous shell, the tunica albuginea, and contain seminiferous tubules where germ cells develop into sperm. Leydig cells between the tubules produce testosterone, while Sertoli cells support sperm development and secrete inhibin. An average adult testicle measures up to 5 cm × 2 cm × 3 cm, and normal volume is 15 to 25 cm³.

Primary male sex hormone and androgen, a [[Steroid|steroid]] derived from [[Cholesterol|cholesterol]]. It drives development of male reproductive tissues such as the [[Testicle|testicles]] and [[Prostate|prostate]], and promotes secondary sexual characteristics such as increased muscle and bone mass and body hair. In both sexes it influences mood, cognition, metabolism and the prevention of osteoporosis. It is produced mainly by the testicles in males and, to a lesser extent, by the [[Ovary|ovaries]] in females, and adult males have about seven to eight times as much as adult females. It is used as a medication to treat hypogonadism and breast cancer, and older men are sometimes given it to counteract declining levels. It is also used illicitly to enhance physique and performance, and the World Anti-Doping Agency lists it as "prohibited at all times".
